title: Greeks arrive
hook: Alexander reaches the land, and Greek culture spreads

segments.voice: Yesterday we stepped off the last page of the Tanakh, and a chain of teachers picked it up. Your line was the pages ran out; the handing-on didn't. Today, a king from Macedonia.

The first book of Maccabees opens at a gallop. Alexander, son of Philip, the Macedonian, comes out of the land the book calls Chettiim, defeats Darius, king of the Persians. He takes cities, kills kings, and goes to the ends of the earth, until, in the King James words, "the earth was quiet before him." Soon he falls sick, knows he is dying, and divides his kingdom among his servants. He reigned twelve years, the book says. A storm that passes. But what he left behind did not pass: Greek language, Greek cities, Greek ways of living arrive in the land of Israel and stay.
screen: `A KING FROM MACEDONIA.` → `THE EARTH WAS QUIET BEFORE HIM.` → `THE STORM PASSES. THE CULTURE STAYS.`

segments.voice: The Talmud, in tractate Yoma, tells the meeting as a legend. Alexander's army is marching toward Jerusalem. The high priest, Shimon the Righteous, puts on his priestly garments and, with the city's leaders carrying torches, walks all night to meet him. When Alexander sees him, the conqueror gets down from his chariot and bows. His men are shocked. Alexander explains: this is the face I see before me when I win my battles. The Temple is spared. Two worlds meet, and the surprise is who bows. Shimon the Righteous is the man Pirkei Avot names right after the Great Assembly, the one who said the world stands on three things: Torah, service, and acts of loving-kindness. So the legend puts the heir of the chain face to face with the man who conquered the world. But meeting isn't always bowing. In the first book of Maccabees, some in Israel say, let's make a covenant with the nations around us, and they build a place of exercise in Jerusalem after the customs of the nations. The book is not pleased. Two cultures meet, and the meeting goes in every direction: respect, borrowing, worry, conflict. The Hebrew name for Greece, Yavan, turns up in the book of Daniel too: the kingdom of Yavan comes after Persia. The question for the next few days: how do you live inside someone else's culture and stay yourself?
screen: `THE CONQUEROR BOWS.` · then, large: `TORAH, SERVICE, LOVING-KINDNESS.` · `A PLACE OF EXERCISE IN JERUSALEM.` · `INSIDE A CULTURE, STILL YOURSELF?`

segments.voice: Walk through an ordinary day in your mind, the gym, a class, a word you use, and find one thing you suspect came from Greek culture; if you're not sure, just hold the question. Then find one thing from your own family, people or tradition, and let both sit side by side without picking a winner. If you pray, use words from your tradition for the places you live.
Greeks arrive. Alexander sweeps through, and Greek language and ways of life settle into the land of Israel. Today's word.
Your line: two cultures meet. Sometimes the meeting is a bow, sometimes a quarrel. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jewish students learn the saying of Shimon the Righteous in Pirkei Avot, that the world stands on Torah, service and acts of loving-kindness, and the Talmud's legend of his meeting with Alexander is told in study of the Second Temple period.

chat.says: When Alexander's Greeks came, did Jewish life just clash with Greek ways?
options: Every way at once: respect, borrowing, worry, fighting, and a story of Alexander bowing down.
Jews simply rejected everything Greek, and nobody in Israel adopted Greek ways.
Everyone welcomed Greek ways, and no one in Israel was troubled by them.
chat.meaning: The Talmud tells of Alexander bowing to Shimon the Righteous, while 1 Maccabees shows some in Israel adopting the nations' customs: the meeting went every direction.

notes: Claims rule: the outline's '332 BCE' was cut. 'Reigned twelve years' is from 1 Maccabees 1:7.
1 Maccabees is not part of the Tanakh; it is quoted here from the KJV Apocrypha as a historical source. Please verify the exact KJV wording 'the earth was quiet before him' (1:3).

Yoma 69a legend (Shimon HaTzadik meets Alexander; Alexander bows and says he saw this face before battles) paraphrased and framed as legend; Josephus (Antiquities 11.8) tells a version with the high priest Jaddua. Please confirm the details (torches, priestly garments).
Daniel 8:21: Hebrew 'melech Yavan' (KJV 'the king of Grecia'); 'the kingdom of Yavan comes after Persia' paraphrases Daniel 8:20–21. Please confirm.
The 'place of exercise' (gymnasium) is from 1 Maccabees 1:14.
